newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BSC growth seen above 20 pct to 2000.
newsitem.headline: BSC growth seen above 20 pct to 2000.

text.p: Annual business growth at medical device manufacturer Boston Scientific Corporation (BSC) is predicted to remain well above 20 percent to the turn of the century, a top executive said on Monday.
"We expect to continue growing in the mid or upper 20s as a percent of revenue over the next three to five years," Jim Corbett, BSC International Organisation president, told Reuters on Monday.
Corbett said operations outside the U.S. contributed about 40 percent of BSC's US$1.5 billion turnover and would be 50 percent by 2000, fuelled by business from the Asia-Pacific region.
Corbett said Asia-Pacific's medical device market was about US$200-US$300 million, but the potential was many times that.

"We expect this to be the fastest growing area of the world for the company over the next few years," Corbett told a news conference marking the award to BSC's Singapore unit of Business Headquarters status by the Singapore Economic Development Board.
The special status qualifies BSC for tax and other breaks for up to 10 years.

BSC will manage about 100 staff in sales, marketing, distribution and financial operations for Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Taiwan, Korean, Hong Kong, China, Thailand, India, Australia and New Zealand from its Singapore base.

Corbett told Reuters after the news conference that BSC had "invested several million (U.S.) dollars in Singapore", but would give no figure for the return expected, other than to say it would be "better than the corporate average".
The centre could also be used to modify its U.S.-made products to suit Asian needs. Corbett said this could result in some materials being sourced locally.
